claims.text: Average valence electron count predominantly controls Tc in titanium-rich, single-phase disordered HEAs.
Average valence electron count predominantly controls Hc2 in titanium-rich, single-phase disordered HEAs.
Large lattice distortions moderate the influence of VEC on superconducting properties.
Atomic-size mismatch between Ti and heavy transition metals produces large lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions modify electron–phonon coupling.
Lattice distortions modify the density of states at the Fermi level.
Changes in VEC alter electron–phonon coupling strength.
Changes in electron–phonon coupling and Fermi-level density of states set Tc and Hc2.
Powder metallurgy or high-energy mechanical milling followed by sintering can ensure uniform disorder without secondary phases in the proposed alloy.
Most well-studied type-A HEA superconductors contain large amounts of Nb and Ta and generally less than 20 at.% Ti.
Ta0.34Nb0.33Hf0.08Zr0.14Ti0.11 is a superconducting HEA associated with the approximately 4–9 K Tc range of type-A HEA superconductors.
The stated Nb–Ta benchmark has established electron–phonon coupling parameters.
Increasing Ti content will increase lattice distortion in the proposed compositional series.
Greater lattice distortion and heavier-element content may reduce the density of states.
Greater disorder will introduce increased electronic scattering.
Relative to the Nb–Ta benchmark, titanium-rich alloys will likely exhibit a moderate decrease or a non-monotonic change in Tc.
Relative to the Nb–Ta benchmark, titanium-rich alloys will exhibit a change in Hc2.
Tc across the proposed titanium-content series will correlate with computed VEC.
Tc across the proposed titanium-content series will correlate with measured lattice strain.
Compositional disorder can suppress or enhance Tc, so disorder-induced effects may complicate the proposed trend.

contradictions.description: The intervention allows the other elemental fractions to vary within a range, whereas the falsification design says Ti atomic percent will be varied while all other elemental concentrations remain constant. Atomic percentages must sum to 100%, so Ti cannot vary if every other atomic percentage is fixed.
